memory_update.text: AMKR should remain the US-listed OSAT reference anchor for the HBM/backend packaging overflow node, but its direct HBM exposure is not yet proven from primary evidence.
FORM is a strong underfollowed HBM test candidate because official materials explicitly connect its probe-card products to HBM3 and SK hynix HBM testing.
COHU is a strong underfollowed HBM inspection/test candidate because official disclosures explicitly identify a Neon HBM inspection metrology win and broader test-handler/contactors exposure.
ONTO is a broader advanced-packaging metrology and inspection candidate; keep it in the universe but require revenue-mix evidence to avoid over-attributing generic process-control exposure to HBM.

The likely chokepoint map for US-listed names is: OSAT capacity and onshoring anchor AMKR; HBM wafer/probe testing FORM; HBM inspection and thermal/backend test COHU; advanced-packaging process control ONTO.

Need a later non-US-listed pass for Powertech, SPIL/ASE, Ibiden, Shinko, Unimicron, WinWay, Chunghwa Precision Test, TSE, and other Asian substrate/probe/test/socket names because the purest HBM backend exposure may sit outside the US-listed universe.

node: HBM, advanced packaging, and outsourced memory backend packaging/testing overflow
summary: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around HBM-driven backend packaging and test constraints. The cleanest underfollowed lane is not the HBM producers themselves, but OSAT capacity, wafer/probe-card testing, HBM inspection/metrology, thermal test handlers, contactors, and advanced-packaging process-control tools. The strongest US-listed candidates found in this pass are AMKR, FORM, COHU, and ONTO. AMKR is the closest US-listed outsourced packaging/test anchor; FORM and COHU are more targeted test/inspection chokepoint suppliers; ONTO is a broader advanced-packaging metrology and inspection beneficiary. These are research candidates only, not buy/sell recommendations.
